questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes what a variable is in programming?
options: A named location in memory that stores a value for retrieval and updates
A permanent hardware chip on the motherboard that cannot be changed
A special key on the keyboard that opens Python
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! A variable is a named storage container in memory used to hold data.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. A variable is a named location in memory used to store and manipulate data.

questions.question: Which statement correctly stores a person's city name?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! The variable name goes on the left, '=' in the middle, and the text string in quotes on the right.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Variable names go on the left, values on the right, and text strings must be enclosed in quotes.

questions.question: What is the difference between `total = 25` and `total = "25"`?
options: total = 25 is an integer (number for math), while total = "25" is a text string
They are 100% identical in every way
total = 25 is an error in Python
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Without quotes it is an integer (numeric); with quotes it is a string (text).
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Quotes define a string (text), whereas digits without quotes define an integer (number).

questions.question: What will be printed when this script runs?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! `a = b` copies the value of b (10) into a. So printing a outputs 10.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. `a = b` assigns the value of b (which is 10) into a, so `print(a)` outputs 10.

questions.question: What will `print("player")` display if you already wrote `player = "Alex"`?
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Because "player" is wrapped in quotes, print() prints the literal characters 'player', ignoring the variable.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. Quotes mean 'print this literal text'. To print the variable's value, write `print(player)` without quotes.

questions.question: What is the output of the following 4-line program?
options: 1 on the first line, 2 on the second line
questions.explanation_correct: Correct! Python executes in sequential order: Line 2 prints 1, Line 3 updates count to 2, Line 4 prints 2.
questions.explanation_incorrect: Incorrect. The program executes top-to-bottom, printing 1 first and then 2 after the reassignment.
